slides.heading: Knight Connection
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Arrays
slides.narration: Let's solve Knight Connection, a hard arrays problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Two knights on an infinite board move alternately/together; minimum number of turns for them to meet = ceil(knight-move distance / 2).
BFS from one knight to the other.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Two knights on an infinite board move alternately or together; minimum number of turns for them to meet equals ceil(knight-move distance / 2). BFS from one knight to the other.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Knights cover two cells per joint turn, so compute the minimum knight moves to close the gap, then halve it rounding up.
slides.narration: Knights cover two cells per joint turn, so compute the minimum knight moves to close the gap, then halve it rounding up.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Move both knights simultaneously → state space squared
BFS from one knight to the other, halve (round up) → O(d²) cells
Infinite board: no bounds, use a seen set
slides.narration: Searching over both knights' positions squares the state space. Instead, BFS from one knight to the other, then halve the distance, rounding up, since both move each turn.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. BFS knight moves from the origin to the offset between knights
3. Answer is ceiling of moves over two
slides.narration: Step by step. First, bFS knight moves from the origin to the offset between knights. Second, count moves needed. Third, answer is ceiling of moves over two.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We BFS from the first knight, storing x, y and distance. When we dequeue the second knight's square, we return distance plus one over two.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of d squared for distance d. Space is O of d squared.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Round odd distances up. The board is infinite, so a seen set is essential.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: Bidirectional BFS from both knights would explore far fewer squares.
